channel.title: Water Capital Wire
channel.description: A free daily read on the business of water for managers, investors and operators: capital, companies, technology, infrastructure and water security, with every fact sourced and dated.

item.title: Durham has paid over $4 million for borrowed water as North Carolina's drought reaches 6.2 million people
item.description: North Carolina's drought now reaches 6.2 million people. Durham had 76 days of easily accessible water on November 17 and has paid more than $4 million for 898 million gallons bought from Cary and OWASA, because it has no plant of its own on Jordan Lake.

item.title: Nevada's data center boom could need about 34,000 acre-feet of water a year, most of it at power plants
item.description: An updated Desert Research Institute study says proposed Nevada data centers could use about 12,800 acre-feet of water a year for cooling by 2036, and about 21,300 more at the power plants that supply them. Supply will come from groundwater, reclamation or transfers.

item.title: Abu Dhabi will put water investment on the UN agenda for the first time since 2023
item.description: The UN Water Conference opens in Abu Dhabi on December 8, the first UN water summit since 2023, with investment for water as one of its six dialogues. It ends with a President's summary, not a negotiated text, so the deals signed around it matter most.
